lines.text: Two players race to write zero. The twist: for some numbers, the SECOND player can always win!
lines.caption: Two players race to write zero. The twist: for some numbers, the SECOND player can always win!

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's crack this game by working up from zero.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's crack this game by working up from zero.

lines.text: A number n is on the board. On each turn, you take away one, or halve it, rounding down.
lines.caption: A number n is on the board. On each turn, you take away one, or halve it, rounding down.

lines.text: Two players take turns. The player who writes zero wins.
lines.caption: Two players take turns. The player who writes zero wins.

lines.text: For how many n from one to one hundred can the second player always win? Here are the choices.
lines.caption: For how many n from one to one hundred can the second player always win? Here are the choices.

lines.text: We want the numbers where the player to move is stuck. Let's call them losing numbers.
lines.caption: We want the numbers where the player to move is stuck. Let's call them losing numbers.

lines.text: Our job: count the losing numbers from one to one hundred.
lines.caption: Our job: count the losing numbers from one to one hundred.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's start small and make a table.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's start small and make a table.

lines.text: Red means the player to move loses. Green means the player to move wins.
lines.caption: Red means the player to move loses. Green means the player to move wins.

lines.text: Zero is red. If zero is on the board at your turn, your opponent already won.
lines.caption: Zero is red. If zero is on the board at your turn, your opponent already won.

lines.text: From one, you write zero and win. So one is green.
lines.caption: From one, you write zero and win. So one is green.

lines.text: From two, both moves give one, a green for your opponent. So two is red!
lines.caption: From two, both moves give one, a green for your opponent. So two is red!

lines.text: The rule: green if SOME move reaches a red. Red if EVERY move reaches a green.
lines.caption: The rule: green if SOME move reaches a red. Red if EVERY move reaches a green.

lines.text: Three, four and five can each reach two. All green! Six only reaches five or three. Red!
lines.caption: Three, four and five can each reach two. All green! Six only reaches five or three. Red!

lines.text: Keep going up to sixteen. The red numbers are two, six, eight, ten and fourteen.
lines.caption: Keep going up to sixteen. The red numbers are two, six, eight, ten and fourteen.

lines.text: So far, every red number is even. But four, twelve and sixteen are even AND green. Why?
lines.caption: So far, every red number is even. But four, twelve and sixteen are even AND green. Why?

lines.text: Let's count the twos in each number. Six is two times three. That's one two.
lines.caption: Let's count the twos in each number. Six is two times three. That's one two.

lines.text: Eight has three twos. But four and twelve have two twos, and sixteen has four.
lines.caption: Eight has three twos. But four and twelve have two twos, and sixteen has four.

lines.text: There's the pattern! Red numbers have an ODD number of twos: one, three, five, and so on.
lines.caption: There's the pattern! Red numbers have an ODD number of twos: one, three, five, and so on.

lines.text: A pattern isn't proof yet. Let's check that it always holds.
lines.caption: A pattern isn't proof yet. Let's check that it always holds.

lines.text: Take a red number, like eight. Take away one, and you get an odd number, with zero twos.
lines.caption: Take a red number, like eight. Take away one, and you get an odd number, with zero twos.

lines.text: Zero is even, so that's green. Or halve it, and you lose exactly one two. Odd turns even: green!
lines.caption: Zero is even, so that's green. Or halve it, and you lose exactly one two. Odd turns even: green!

lines.text: So from a red number, every move hands your opponent a green.
lines.caption: So from a red number, every move hands your opponent a green.

lines.text: From a green even number, like twelve, halving drops one two. Even turns odd, so six is red!
lines.caption: From a green even number, like twelve, halving drops one two. Even turns odd, so six is red!

lines.text: From an odd number, like thirteen, you can reach twelve, or half of twelve, which is six.
lines.caption: From an odd number, like thirteen, you can reach twelve, or half of twelve, which is six.

lines.text: Those two differ by one two, so one count is odd. Hand over that red! From one, just write zero.
lines.caption: Those two differ by one two, so one count is odd. Hand over that red! From one, just write zero.

lines.text: Count the reds by their twos. One two: fifty evens, minus twenty-five multiples of four. Twenty-five!
lines.caption: Count the reds by their twos. One two: fifty evens, minus twenty-five multiples of four. Twenty-five!

lines.text: Three twos: eight, twenty-four, forty, fifty-six, seventy-two, eighty-eight. Six!
lines.caption: Three twos: eight, twenty-four, forty, fifty-six, seventy-two, eighty-eight. Six!

lines.text: Five twos: thirty-two and ninety-six. Seven twos starts at one hundred twenty-eight, too big.
lines.caption: Five twos: thirty-two and ninety-six. Seven twos starts at one hundred twenty-eight, too big.

lines.text: Twenty-five plus six plus two. The answer is <short pause> thirty-three! Choice C.
lines.caption: Twenty-five plus six plus two. The answer is thirty-three! Choice C.

lines.text: Here's a slicker way to count. What happens when you double a number?
lines.caption: Here's a slicker way to count. What happens when you double a number?

lines.text: Doubling adds exactly one two. So it flips the count from odd to even, or even to odd.
lines.caption: Doubling adds exactly one two. So it flips the count from odd to even, or even to odd.

lines.text: So the reds up to one hundred are exactly the doubles of the greens up to fifty.
lines.caption: So the reds up to one hundred are exactly the doubles of the greens up to fifty.

lines.text: And the greens up to fifty are fifty, minus the reds up to fifty.
lines.caption: And the greens up to fifty are fifty, minus the reds up to fifty.

lines.text: Use the same trick again and again, halving and rounding down: fifty, twenty-five, twelve, six, three, one. The signs take turns.
lines.caption: Use the same trick again and again, halving and rounding down: fifty, twenty-five, twelve, six, three, one. The signs take turns.

lines.text: Fifty minus twenty-five, plus twelve, minus six, plus three, minus one. Thirty-three again!
lines.caption: Fifty minus twenty-five, plus twelve, minus six, plus three, minus one. Thirty-three again!

lines.text: It's handy when the range is huge, like one to a million.
lines.caption: It's handy when the range is huge, like one to a million.

lines.text: Choice A, twenty-five, is what you'd get if you only counted numbers with exactly one two.
lines.caption: Choice A, twenty-five, is what you'd get if you only counted numbers with exactly one two.

lines.text: Choice B, thirty-one, is what you'd get if you missed thirty-two and ninety-six. Five twos is odd too!
lines.caption: Choice B, thirty-one, is what you'd get if you missed thirty-two and ninety-six. Five twos is odd too!

lines.text: Choice D, thirty-four, is what you'd get if you counted one as red. But from one, you write zero and win.
lines.caption: Choice D, thirty-four, is what you'd get if you counted one as red. But from one, you write zero and win.

lines.text: Choice E, fifty, is what you'd get if every even number were red. But four goes to two, so four is green.
lines.caption: Choice E, fifty, is what you'd get if every even number were red. But four goes to two, so four is green.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. Always build a table first, then trust the pattern only after you prove it.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. Always build a table first, then trust the pattern only after you prove it.

scenes.chapter: Your turn: one to two hundred

lines.text: Your turn: same game, from one to two hundred. How many can the second player always win?
lines.caption: Your turn: same game, from one to two hundred. How many can the second player always win?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Halve two hundred again and again: one hundred, fifty, twenty-five, twelve, six, three, one.
lines.caption: Halve two hundred again and again: one hundred, fifty, twenty-five, twelve, six, three, one.

lines.text: One hundred minus fifty, plus twenty-five, minus twelve, plus six, minus three, plus one. That's <short pause> sixty-seven!
lines.caption: One hundred minus fifty, plus twenty-five, minus twelve, plus six, minus three, plus one. That's sixty-seven!

lines.text: Check by groups: fifty, plus thirteen, plus three, plus one more for the number one hundred twenty-eight. Sixty-seven!
lines.caption: Check by groups: fifty, plus thirteen, plus three, plus one more for the number one hundred twenty-eight. Sixty-seven!

lines.text: The big idea: in a take-turns game, find the losing spots for small numbers. Spot a pattern.
lines.caption: The big idea: in a take-turns game, find the losing spots for small numbers. Spot a pattern.

lines.text: Then prove it: every move from red goes to green, and some move from green goes to red.
lines.caption: Then prove it: every move from red goes to green, and some move from green goes to red.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
